blueprint.notes: Alumni Hall 680211974: July 2012 geolocated ENE/South Avenue Street View supports the faceted central bay and open hipped-cap balcony. Native balcony deck rests on the bay and its back roof intersects the main hip. Lower veranda stays within the main facade span. Remove unsupported attic wall openings left above the north hip; the May 2023 rear image is heavily obstructed and does not support dormers there.

Lakefront facade correction: dedicated decorated square veranda columns, paired arched entrance transom above retained double-door leaf, terrain-fitted splayed stairs and roof flag. Generic lakefront/wing porch specifications remain as frontage metadata; their geometry is replaced by the native Athenaeum front renderer. Other facades, barrel canopy and existing building frame remain unchanged.

Hall-facing elevation corrected from user photograph supplied 2026-09-14: recessed covered gallery under the enclosed upper storey, supported above the lower level, and a narrow open timber stair along the wall at the gallery end. Removed the 15-step outward-projecting stair aimed at Smith Wilkes Hall. The other elevations and existing main entrance remain from the previous blueprint. Dimensions estimated from the supplied photograph.

blueprint.notes: Corrected from user-supplied Bestor Plaza corner Street View, 2026-09-14. Four open upper arches on the +v Miller Avenue front; two-storey veranda continues along +u around the rounded entrance corner. One main hip covers both verandas. Pale yellow siding, cream rails, green post caps, curved Hultquist Center nameplate and red-white-blue bunting. Rear wings retain existing inferred massing; dimensions are visual estimates within the mapped footprint.

Bestor Plaza memorial fountain: four shallow stone allegories with their identifying attributes and inscriptions, ART (palette and brush), RELIGION (bearded figure holding tablet), KNOWLEDGE (torch and scroll), MUSIC (lyre). Native fountain renderer provides fluted corner pilasters, palmette frieze and stepped crown. Preserve the existing 11 m square basin, 4.9 m height and four corner jets. Art/Religion adjacency follows the supplied corner reference; absolute compass assignments are not established by the unlocated close-up photographs. Four corner statuettes are carved fish with raised heads, forked tails, fins and overlapping scales; each open mouth is aligned to its inward water jet. Water, coping, pylon and fish structure are retained in coarse streaming scenery.

Grounded in June 2026 Street View and cached Esri aerial. Cream script sign is native CanvasTexture; current front entry has no brown dome awning. Roof heights, hidden rear openings, and patio furniture are miniature approximations.
